defects: Primary blocker — B-BARE exposes an implausibly congested scaffold of many near-parallel upright stems, crossing branches, and conspicuously blunt/cut-looking upper tips. This does not match the reference's legible hierarchy of trunk, major limbs, and progressively finer ramification, and it is an obvious construction artifact affecting species believability. Because B-WHOLE and B-BARE share seed-1 geometry, foliage merely conceals this defect rather than resolving it.
observations: B-WHOLE has a believable dense, tall ovoid deciduous crown and smooth pale-gray bark consistent with European beech reference character.
The candidate's multi-stem lower architecture is acceptable natural variation: the references include both single-trunk and multi-stem specimens, with no documented same-specimen relationship.

The candidate meets the accepted anchor's stylized catalogue finish floor in general rendering coherence; photorealistic bark, leaves, lighting, and background integration are optional refinements and do not block readiness.
The photographic references show different, undocumented specimen or condition relationships; no causal seasonal or developmental relationship was inferred.

findings.observation: Required cell B-WHOLE/reference_character passes: render-0 matches reference-0 in its dense leafy deciduous mass, tall rounded-to-ovoid crown, and smooth light-gray beech-like trunk; differences in exact crown spread and stem count remain plausible specimen variation.

Required cell B-BARE/reference_character fails: render-1 is dominated by an excessively dense bundle of similarly upright, intersecting axes with numerous abruptly terminated tips, whereas reference-1 presents a readable primary scaffold and finer outward ramification. The mismatch removes defining structural character and introduces obvious construction artifacts.
findings.causal_hypothesis: The generator may be producing too many competing upright axes and/or terminating branches before natural taper and subdivision are established; this is optional and not required to sustain the observed mismatch.

findings.observation: Cross-view constraint: render-0 and render-1 share identity, seed, and geometry; the foliage shown in render-0 hides much of the defective scaffold visible in render-1 and cannot be treated as alternative unloaded leaf-off geometry.

Against the finish-only catalogue anchor, the candidate has coherent materials, lighting, silhouette presentation, and comparable or greater visible detail; the blocker is structural character rather than a general finish-floor regression.
